_about: Gemini 3.5 Flash drafted these answers (ungrounded) on 2 Nov 2026 from Abbas's context. Claude rewrote each one the same day, keeping the voice and structure but replacing every fact that conflicted with official pages or the board. 'fixed' lists what changed from Gemini's draft.

imperial-pres.tag: Round 1 has closed: round 2 on 11 Jan, and only with a supervisor
imperial-pres.lede: The Imperial College President's PhD Scholarships are the most prestigious doctoral funding Imperial offers. They're fully funded and a real route into world-class research. Round 1 closed on 2 Nov, so the live chance is round 2 on **11 Jan 2027**, and without a supervisor's agreement you're not ready for it.

us: A 3.5-year PhD pushes a US Match out to about 2031–32.
eu: Great for UK research networks, but it doesn't license you to practise.
interest: Public health, epidemiology and global health departments all sit here.

ul: **Full tuition fees** at the overseas rate.
**£27,036 a year** tax-free stipend for up to 3.5 years, plus **£2,000 a year** for research costs.
About **50 awards** a year, open to any nationality.
Your **$30,000 budget stays untouched**: it can go to USMLE fees and US clinical experience instead.
Any nationality, Bangladesh included.
A **first-class degree or equivalent**. How Imperial reads an MBBS comes down to your marks and class rank.
A **supervisor's agreement first**: find a faculty member in an area like the School of Public Health, email them your CV and a short proposal, and get their yes before you apply.
**Round 1: closed 2 Nov 2026** (decisions by 31 Jan 2027).
**Round 2: 11 Jan 2027.** Round 3: 1 Mar 2027.
Funded 2027–28 places can start as late as **1 Nov 2027**, which brushes against the end of your internship.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A PhD from Imperial in public health makes you exceptionally competitive for academic residency programmes, and London gives you a base for PLAB and NHS contacts. But the plan that works for 2029 is Step 1 during the internship, a paid US research job, then Step 2 CK. A 3.5-year PhD replaces that plan rather than adding to it, and your Match year moves to roughly 2031–32.

ul: **Catch 1: timing.** Round 1 has closed. Round 2 on 11 Jan 2027 is the realistic target, and you need an agreed supervisor before then.
**Catch 2: competition.** Fifty awards across the whole college, usually for people with research experience. A fresh MBBS with no publications needs a strong supervisor connection.
**Catch 3: years since graduation.** Many US programmes screen on how long ago you graduated. A PhD explains the gap well for academic programmes, less so for community ones.
**Catch 4: clinical distance.** Three and a half years in a research group means arranging observerships before you reapply to residency.

p: Treat this as a **physician-scientist route**, not a 2029 route. Apply in round 2 if a supervisor commits in the next two months. Otherwise keep your energy on Step 1 and a paid US research post.

fixed: Stipend: Gemini said £25,150 (2024/25). The current figure on the board is £27,036 a year.
Rounds: Gemini gave 4 Nov / 8 Jan / 13 Mar. The real rounds are 2 Nov 2026, 11 Jan 2027 and 1 Mar 2027.
Timeline: Gemini had you finishing the internship in late 2026. It runs from about Oct–Nov 2026 to late 2027, so the 1 Nov 2027 latest start matters.
Removed unverified claims about Imperial's space-agency links.
Round 1 wording: the original draft said Round 1 closes today. It closed on 2 Nov 2026, so the route now points to round 2 on 11 Jan 2027.

oist-phd.tag: Brilliant funding, wrong field for epidemiology
oist-phd.lede: OIST is an elite, English-language graduate university on Okinawa with one of the most generous PhD packages anywhere. It's basic science and computation rather than public health, so the question is whether you'd want a lab life for five years.

us: Five years in basic science puts a Match at about 2033.
eu: No help with licensing in the UK, Germany or Ireland.
interest: Neuroscience, genetics and computational biology yes; epidemiology no.

p: A single 5-year integrated PhD. The first two years are lab rotations and coursework, and the last three are thesis research. There are no departments: units cover molecular and cell biology, neuroscience, mathematics and computation, chemistry, physics and ecology.

ul: Tuition included, with a stipend of about **¥2.6 million a year**, rising to about ¥3.6 million.
Support for relocation and conference travel.
**Cost to apply: ¥5,000**, non-refundable and without waivers. It's small, but it isn't free.
Completion of a **bachelor's, master's or equivalent** before the admission date. Medicine isn't named, so confirm with admissions that an MBBS is accepted.
Check that your chosen unit actually has room to supervise new PhD students. OIST warns that strong applicants are rejected when the field has no space.
**15 Nov 2026, 23:59 JST** for the 2027 admissions workshop round.
Entry on 1 May or 1 Sep 2027, or **1 Jan 2028**. The January 2028 entry is the one that fits the end of your internship.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A PhD with strong papers helps for academic residencies, but US programmes weigh clinical experience and clinical research more heavily than bench work. Europe's licensing routes (PLAB, the German Kenntnisprüfung, Ireland's PRES) don't change at all.

ul: **Catch 1: timeline.** Starting in 2028 and finishing five years later puts a US Match at roughly 2033.
**Catch 2: field mismatch.** There is no public health or epidemiology unit. Computational biology is your closest door.
**Catch 3: admission.** Research experience matters a lot, and you'd be competing with people who have lab degrees.

p: Apply only if you're deliberately choosing a research career and would lean into computational work. For a Match-focused plan, skip it.

fixed: Application fee: Gemini said $0. OIST charges ¥5,000, non-refundable, no waivers (confirmed on oist.jp).
Stipend: Gemini said about ¥2.4 million; the board and OIST's package point to about ¥2.6 million.
Removed a second April application cycle and the GRE and acceptance-rate claims, none of which could be confirmed.

sanger-phd.tag: Exceptional if you can show genomics and coding skills
sanger-phd.lede: The Wellcome Sanger Institute 4-year PhD is one of the best-funded doctorates in the world, with a Cambridge degree at the end. It's a genomics and data-science programme, so it only works if that's the work you want.

us: Four years pushes a Match to about 2032.
eu: Strong UK academic standing; no licensing shortcut.
interest: Genomic epidemiology yes; policy, health economics and aerospace no.

p: A 1+3 model. In year one you do three short rotations in different labs plus taught modules, then choose your main project. The degree is awarded by the University of Cambridge, and you work on the Wellcome Genome Campus.

ul: **Full university tuition fees** and a stipend (£25,270 in year one at Oct 2025 rates).
Visa and NHS surcharge costs reimbursed.
At least **12 funded studentships**, whatever your nationality.
**Cost to apply:** nothing for the Sanger application. If selected, the Cambridge admission application costs **£20**.
Candidates expected to hold a **1st or good 2:1**, or an equivalent overseas qualification. Whether your MBBS is read that way is worth asking.
Genomics and data science are the focus. Basic Python or R and some statistics will help an MBBS profile a lot.
**24 Nov 2026, 09:00 GMT** is the closing time.
Start is in October 2027, which is likely to collide with your internship: ask whether a later start is possible before spending time on the application.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A Cambridge-linked PhD with strong genomics papers is a great physician-scientist credential and can put you in contact with US collaborators for letters. It doesn't give you US clinical experience, and a four-year PhD moves a Match to around 2032.

ul: **Catch 1: scope.** This is genomics and computation, not general public health.
**Catch 2: preparation.** Selection favours people with coding or lab skills you may not have built yet.
**Catch 3: clinical distance.** Four years away from patients means rebuilding clinical credibility afterwards.

p: If genomic epidemiology really pulls you, ask Sanger about starting later and whether an MBBS qualifies, and spend the internship building Python and R skills. If the 2029 Match is the priority, this isn't the route.

eth-esop.tag: Fully funded, but not a road to a medical licence
eth-esop.lede: ETH Zurich's Excellence Scholarship (ESOP) pays for a Master's at one of Europe's top technical universities, with a real living allowance. It's a science degree, not a licence to practise, and the autumn start sits on top of your internship.

us: Prestige helps, but it adds years without US clinical experience.
eu: Doesn't unlock Swiss or EU medical licensing.
interest: Health Sciences & Technology and statistics fit; no MPH-style courses.

ul: **CHF 13,500 per semester** living allowance plus a tuition waiver.
About 60 awards, based on merit rather than financial need.
**Cost to apply: CHF 150** per programme (non-Swiss degree), non-refundable, no waivers. There's no extra ESOP fee.
Strong results in your degree, roughly the **top 10% of your class**.
A Master's application to ETH for the autumn semester, with a **thesis pre-proposal** you write yourself. That pre-proposal carries a lot of weight.
Typical English requirement is around IELTS 7.0 or TOEFL 100; check your programme's page.
The window is **1–30 Nov 2026**, with a September 2027 start. That start collides with the internship, so ask about a later one or plan for the next cycle.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: An ETH MSc in health sciences, statistics or biomedical engineering looks excellent on a residency application, and it links to aerospace physiology research. What it can't do is give you US clinical experience or any shortcut to practise in Switzerland or the EU, where you'd still need the local recognition exams and the language.

ul: **Catch 1: competition.** You need rank and a strong research idea, not just good marks.
**Catch 2: course fit.** ETH's health degrees are quantitative and molecular; there's no standard MPH.
**Catch 3: timeline.** One and a half to two years away from the USMLE track pushes a Match to about 2031.

p: Apply only if you want a quantitative research career and can write a convincing thesis pre-proposal. For a clinical Match, skip it. For European practice, Germany's Kenntnisprüfung or the UK's PLAB are more direct.

fixed: Living allowance: Gemini said CHF 12,000 per semester. The board has CHF 13,500.
Class rank: Gemini said top 10% in one answer and top 1–2% in another. ESOP's criterion is about the top 10%.
Application fee: Gemini said nothing; ETH charges CHF 150 per programme.
Timeline: Gemini had you finishing the internship in late 2026. It runs to late 2027, so the September 2027 start collides with it.

yenching.tag: Free, prestigious, but it's a China Studies degree
yenching.lede: The Yenching Academy at Peking University is a fully funded two-year Master's, often compared to a Rhodes or Marshall. It's an interdisciplinary China Studies degree, so it works as a global-health-policy credential rather than medical training.

us: A CV booster and a gap-explainer, with no clinical value.
eu: Helps global-health and policy careers, not licensing.
interest: Health policy via Society & Culture or Politics tracks; no epidemiology methods.

ul: Tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one round-trip fare and field-study costs.
No application fee is listed. Applying is free.
A bachelor's degree in any field, or someone currently enrolled and expecting a diploma by August of the intake year.
**English: IELTS 7.0 minimum.** Scores must be sent directly to the Academy.
Two academic letters from full or associate professors in your intended field, a personal statement (750 words) and a research-interest statement (up to 1,500 words).
**30 Nov 2026, 09:00 Beijing time.** Apply early: the closing hour is in the morning, China time.
The September 2027 start collides with your internship, so ask about arriving late or aim for the following year.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: It preserves your $30,000 and gives you a prestigious, well-explained one-to-two years after the MBBS. A thesis on China's health system, global health diplomacy or South Asia–East Asia comparisons would sit well with preventive-medicine programmes. It gives you no US clinical experience, and USMLE preparation will still need dedicated time.

ul: **Catch 1: degree type.** It's a Master of Arts in China Studies, not an MPH or epidemiology degree.
**Catch 2: workload.** Balancing the Academy with Step 1 and Step 2 CK is tough.
**Catch 3: no aerospace medicine.** There's no entry point here.

p: Worth applying if global health policy genuinely interests you and you can build a real thesis around it. If you want methods training, choose an epidemiology programme instead.

clarendon.tag: No form to fill, but your course choice matters
clarendon.lede: The Clarendon Fund is Oxford's flagship full-funding scheme. There's no separate application: you apply for your course, and strong applicants are considered automatically. That makes the course you choose, and when you can arrive, the real decision.

us: A one-year MSc is the only Oxford shape that keeps a 2030 Match realistic.
eu: UK base for PLAB and NHS contacts; no licence on its own.
interest: Global Health Science & Epidemiology is a direct fit.

ul: Full course fees plus a living grant for the whole degree.
A MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology carries overseas fees of about £36,900 (2027–28), so funding it yourself isn't realistic.
**Cost to apply: £75** for taught courses or **£20** for research courses. Applicants resident in a listed low-income country, Bangladesh included, can have it waived.
Any nationality, any subject. Medicine degrees are accepted.
The course deadline is what counts: everyone who applies by it and gets an offer is considered.
**Skip the MSc in International Health and Tropical Medicine:** it asks for 3+ years of low-resource work experience, which you don't have yet.
**1 Dec 2026, 12:00 UK** for the MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology. The Oxford and NDPH pages served older-cycle text on re-check, so confirm on the Graduate Admissions page.
An October 2027 start collides with the internship. The next realistic cycle is December 2027 for October 2028.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A one-year Oxford MSc in epidemiology is the strongest version of an academic credential you can get quickly, and Oxford's population-health groups have US collaborations that can lead to letters. It's still not US clinical experience, and in the UK it doesn't replace PLAB.

ul: **Catch 1: competition.** You can't apply to Clarendon directly. You need a place first, and marks and rank near the top.
**Catch 2: timing.** The cycle that fits your internship is next year's.
**Catch 3: exam clash.** An Oxford MSc plus Step 2 CK preparation in the same year is a heavy load.

p: Apply for the MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology only if you can get a later start or are happy to wait for the 2028 intake. Use the waiver, and never pay course fees from your $30,000.

eu: A funded base in Europe, but it doesn't license you.
interest: Space neuroscience overlaps; epidemiology does not.

About 20 places from 800+ applicants.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A Master's with a good thesis boosts a neurology or neurosurgery application, and living in Germany or France gives you time to learn the language for later licensing. None of it counts as US clinical experience, and time on a two-year programme pushes a US Match out to 2030 or later.

ul: **Catch 1: field.** It's basic and translational neuroscience, not public health.
**Catch 2: competition.** Candidates with lab or coding experience have an edge.
**Catch 3: workload.** Two universities, lab rotations and USMLE preparation is a lot at once.

p: Apply only if neuroscience is a real interest. If epidemiology is the goal, put your motivation letter into Europubhealth+ or IDOH instead.

hkpfs.tag: Among the best fits for your timing, if you can match a PhD to your interests
hkpfs.lede: The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme pays a generous stipend with no nationality, age or work-experience limit, and it allows a deferred start to 31 January 2028. That deferral is why it fits your internship better than most.

us: A multi-year PhD moves a Match well past 2029.
eu: Strong academic credential; no licensing impact.
interest: HKU and CUHK public health schools are global leaders.

ul: **HK$344,400 a year** (about US$44,000) plus **HK$14,400 a year** for travel, for up to three years.
Host universities usually cover the tuition for fellows, but confirm that in your offer: it isn't part of the RGC award.
**Cost to apply:** the initial application is free. Each university's own application costs about **HK$500 per programme**.
Any nationality. No age or work-experience limit.
You choose up to **two programmes at one or two universities**.
You'll need a strong research proposal, references and English scores. The selection panel rates research potential, academic record and leadership.
**1 Dec 2026**: the initial application to the RGC closes at **12:00 noon Hong Kong time**, and university deadlines can follow almost immediately.
Fellows normally start Jul–Sep 2027, but with RGC approval you can defer to **31 January 2028**.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A PhD in infectious-disease epidemiology or public health from HKU or CUHK, with real publications, is a strong credential for academic residency programmes. It doesn't license you in the UK or Europe, and it doesn't replace US clinical experience.

ul: **Catch 1: timeline.** Even a deferred start leaves you several years from a US Match.
**Catch 2: competition.** About 400 fellowships worldwide, and the panel prizes publications.
**Catch 3: no aerospace medicine.** Hong Kong isn't a hub for it.

p: Submit the RGC step by noon on 1 Dec if you want a research career: it's one of the few big PhD schemes that works around an internship. Weigh it carefully against the 2029 plan first.

jhu-phd.tag: Strong funding; ask one question about work experience first
jhu-phd.lede: The Johns Hopkins Bloomberg PhD in Epidemiology is a fully funded, top-ranked programme, and it's one of the few US PhDs that explicitly says a prior graduate degree isn't required. One line about work experience is still unresolved.

us: A 4–5 year PhD moves a US clinical Match to about 2032.
eu: Great for academic and global-health careers, no licensing impact.
interest: Epidemiology and clinical research are exactly this.

You'll need a WES or similar credential evaluation, English scores, a statement of purpose and letters.

**1 Dec 2026** via SOPHAS, for an August 2027 start.
WES evaluation takes weeks, so ask whether the application can go in with WES still in progress. Start it today.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals

ul: **Catch 1: admission.** One of the most competitive PhDs in the field. Most successful applicants have a master's or research track record.
**Catch 2: timing.** August 2027 starts before your internship ends.
**Catch 3: years since graduation.** A PhD finishing around 2031–32 means your MBBS is six years old when you apply.

p: Email the department this week, quoting both work-experience lines. If they say the internship counts and allow a later start, apply. Otherwise, next year's cycle suits your timeline better.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals

interest: Biomedical and data angles only; no clinical track.

A **S$1,000** settling-in allowance and **S$1,500** towards airfare.
No service bond.

International graduates in science and engineering fields at NUS, NTU, SUTD or SMU, supervised through A*STAR.

**1 Dec 2026, 23:59 Singapore time** for the August 2027 intake.
**1 June 2027** for the **January 2028** intake: this is the one that fits your departure window.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A Singapore PhD builds strong biomedical or data skills, and the stipend lets you save money for USMLE costs. It's four years of non-clinical work, so a US Match moves to around 2032, and it does nothing for UK or European licensing.

eu: Great for German research careers, no licensing.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A Max Planck PhD in biomedical AI is a distinctive credential for academic residency programmes. It adds years before any US Match and does nothing for German licensing, where you'd still need the language and the Kenntnisprüfung.

**Catch 2: competition.** Strong research and coding background expected.
**Catch 3: timing.** The fall 2027 start collides with the internship.

p: Worth a look if the new Biomedical AI School excites you and you can build computational skills. Email the School about late starts first.
